content.heading: Browse by topic
content.lead: Every article below is a sample. Together they show what Insights will cover: where to start, what things cost, and how we work with your team.

items.title: Start with the work your team does twice
items.meta: Sample article · Getting started · [3] min read
items.text: Most companies don’t need a big AI plan to begin. They need one task that takes hours every week and follows the same steps each time.

items.title: When AI is not the answer
items.meta: Sample article · Getting started · [3] min read
items.text: Sometimes the fix is a clearer form or one less approval step. We say so, even when it means less work for us.

items.title: Check the AI you already pay for
items.meta: Sample article · Pricing and costs · [4] min read
items.text: Tools like Salesforce and HubSpot include AI features. Before you buy anything new, see what your current plans can already do.

items.title: Questions to ask before you outsource AI work
items.meta: Sample article · Data and trust · [5] min read
items.text: Who reviews the work? Where does your data stay? How will you see progress? What to ask any team, ours included.

items.title: How a time difference turns into overnight progress
items.meta: Sample article · Working together · [4] min read
items.text: Brief us before you log off, and see progress when you log on. For UK partners, our afternoon is your morning.

items.title: What a hire really costs
items.meta: Sample article · Hiring and teams · [5] min read
items.text: Salary is only part of it. Benefits, recruiting and equipment add to it. Compare the full cost before you decide.

notes: Every article is a sample and says so: the hero note, ‘Sample article’ first in every meta line and the ‘Every article below is a sample’ lead. Titles and excerpts come from the Insights email in brand-kit/emails/newsletter.html (lead story ‘Start with the work your team does twice’, short stories ‘When AI is not the answer’ and ‘What a hire really costs’) and from the Brand DNA (the price table and price rules, the buyer questions, the time-zone lines and the ‘AI in tools you already pay for’ service). The featured article is the one written in full on 19 · Article, so its read time (3 min, from its word count) is real; the other read times stay placeholders ([3], [4], [5]) until those articles exist. No figures appear on this page, so it needs no sources; the sourced price table lives in the article. One Primary (Subscribe) in the navy newsletter chapter; the hero’s action is a Secondary that jumps to it, because on a reading page the committing action is the sign-up. Layouts differ section to section: text-led hero, image-left split, zig-zag of lead and short stories, navy product visual. Three new images and one existing email preview; IMG-19-1 is shared with the article page and IMG-18-1 and IMG-18-2 are reused in its related articles, each keeping one ID. The newsletter cadence stays the placeholder [once a month], as on the newsletter-confirmed page. Built 2026-11-03: desktop 75:3655, mobile 76:304; both lint clean (no findings).
